title: Investigate and patch 'throughput bleed' during regional surges impacting TTFT and tokens/sec across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported abrupt TTFT spikes and sustained tokens/sec degradation during regional traffic surges. Symptoms look like a 'throughput bleed' where initial-token latency climbs and steady-state token emission rate drops by 20-60% for affected variants. This ticket coordinates triage, a short-term patch, and follow-up hardening across runtime scheduler, KV cache policy, and kernel-selection heuristics.
observed_metrics: TTFT: +150-1200ms on P50/P95 depending on model and region
fanout tail queue length increased on priming requests
hypothesis_summary: Initial triage indicates a combination of (1) scheduler preemption under surge causing micro-shedder oscillation, (2) aggressive KV cache eviction when multi-model fanout increases, and (3) recent kernel-heuristic rollout (kernel-selector v3) mis-ranking quantized kernels for mid-length contexts. Any single factor could amplify the others leading to the observed throughput bleed.
recent_changes_potentially_related: prefetch reservation default lowered in autoscaler config (2026-03-09)
regional routing weight tweak for eu-west-2 (2026-03-11)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Replay production-like traffic profile using surge-replay job 'surge-replay-20260311' against a staging cluster with mixed-model fanout (rwdl-7b + oss-chat-13b).
2) Ramp to 300% baseline qps over 90s and hold for 10 minutes, ensure priming-heavy sessions are included.
3) Observe scheduler logs for preemption events, KV cache eviction rates, and kernel selection telemetry.
4) Compare token emission rate and TTFT before/after disabling kernel-selector v3 in staging and with prefetched KV credits forced on.
5) Validate on a Private VPC cluster with identical orchestration to reproduce parity issues seen by customer X.

customer_reports: Customer ACME Corp: observed token emission drop in eu-west-2 during marketing surge (support#8472)
Customer HelixAI (Dedicated): reported 30% tokens/sec drop and sustained high P95 (support#8520)
Customer BankCo (Private): similar symptoms after routing change, temporarily mitigated by scaling out instances (support#8555)
priority_rationale: Multiple paying customers affected across deployment types, SLO breaches for TTFT observed in multiple regions, and potential revenue impact if sustained over business-critical surges.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 10:00 - Load-tests in staging reproduced tokens/sec drop when kernel-selector v3 enabled
2026-03-12 11:15 - Forcing KV reservation prevented sustained emission drop but increased memory pressure on workers
2026-03-12 12:30 - Rolling back kernel-selector v3 on a small canary pool restored tokens/sec to baseline
2026-03-13 09:00 - Private cluster showed same behavior; audit shows scheduler preemptions spiked during fanout bursts
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Short-term: roll back kernel-selector v3 for Hosted and Dedicated canaries to restore baseline throughput (tradeoff: lose some perf wins on rare workloads).
Mitigation: enable temporary KV reservation increase for high-fanout pools (tradeoff: higher memory usage/cost).
Long-term: add a kernel-selection A/B probe with safety cap and integrate kernel-selection confidence score into scheduler to avoid preempting low-latency kernels.
proposed_hotfix_steps: 1) Immediately rollback kernel-selector v3 in hosted region canaries (eu-west-2 first).
2) Push configuration change to increase prefetched KV credits for prioritized pools (feature-flagged).
3) Add temporary throttle on model-variant probing frequency to reduce churn in kernel metrics.
4) Notify affected customers and coordinate maintenance window for Dedicated/Private where rollback requires controller restart.

2) tokens/sec sustained drop no longer observed in 15-minute surge-replay runs
3) Customers confirm reduction in observed errors or SLA breaches
4) No memory OOMs triggered by temporary KV reservation increase in canaries
